page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highmem-4 is an x86_64 compute instance engineered for memory-weighted infrastructure demands. The system provision provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. Two execution threads per core provide parallel thread handling backed by 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 105 MB L3 cache pool. The underlying host platform exposes instruction set extensions including AVX, AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, and Advanced Matrix Extensions for specialized vector processing. Memory is provisioned at 32 GB, giving an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation of 8 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local SSD storage, nor does it contain hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating network-attached block storage for persistent data.

In synthetic compute and system evaluations, the c3-highmem-4 exhibits mid-range single-core capability paired with lower multi-core aggregate throughput due to its 2-core physical limit. Single-core stress-ng registered at 1619.48, while multi-core reached 3320.67. Geekbench testing returned a single-core score of 1719.0 and a multi-core score of 3828.0, with clang software compilation scoring 4239.0. Memory throughput evaluations indicate 272.28 GB/s in small cached 16 KB read blocks, descending to 29.09 GB/s for large uncached 256 MB reads and 21.83 GB/s for 256 MB writes. Database and key-value evaluations recorded 2043.21 on PassMark database operations and 4.46 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks. Static web throughput sustained 6.77 GB/s, while language model inference reached 108.8 tokens per second on text generation using a compact 135M parameter model.

The configuration presents architectural tradeoffs centered on its high memory ratio versus lower compute density. For memory-bound processes that do not saturate high core counts, the 32 GB RAM allocation prevents premature provisioning of larger compute shapes, optimizing operational expenditure per gigabyte. Conversely, CPU-intensive tasks such as sustained multi-threaded rendering or heavy compilation face bottlenecks from the 4-vCPU boundary. Absence of bundled local NVMe storage additionally requires relying on network storage throughput for persistence. The instance fits memory-heavy enterprise software, standalone relational databases, caching tiers like Redis or Memcached, static web serving infrastructure, and lightweight model inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-highmem-4 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Built on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, the instance includes 105 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. It operates without integrated local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, requiring persistent disks over network interfaces for non-volatile storage needs. Benchmark testing reflects average single-thread compute capabilities alongside moderate uncached memory bandwidth of 29.09 GB/s read and 21.83 GB/s write. Because total multi-core processing throughput is limited by its 2 physical cores, the instance provides cost-efficient operation primarily when workloads require ample memory headroom rather than intensive continuous parallel CPU execution. It is suited for in-memory caching systems such as Redis, relational databases, static web serving, and memory-constrained microservices.
